pairs.why: Both locomotives are large dark-navy masses, which is heavier than the real cards' small dark accents. B breaks its dark body up with big red mid-value areas (cab roof, wheels, cowcatcher) and sits on a lighter sky. That matches the real cards' bright, mid-key look with a saturated mid-value hero slightly better than A's darker overall mass.

A puts a heavy dark charcoal rim and deep teal slab on the bright yellow ground. That is a hard dark-on-light hero that the real cards don't have, since their darkest accents are small. B's lighter silver hero has gentler internal values and a brighter glow behind it, closer to the real cards' soft separation.
